summary: PulseGuard v0.6.39 fixes stability scoring/watermark logic, WinGet source validation, application executable ownership, CPU accounting, startup safety, cleanup policy, Game Ready explanations, report serialization/size, RAM labels, and repeated NotApplicable update noise.

sections.heading: Crash history can no longer be self-resolved
sections.detail: Event-backed BSOD, WHEA, shutdown, GPU, storage and repeated-crash history can no longer be cleared by generic maintenance, a post-scan, or unrelated driver/vendor activity. Only an explicitly mapped targeted repair may start a verification window; simply finding sppsvc already running is verification only and does not count as a repair. Existing pre-v0.6.39 generic watermarks are ignored, and repaired event history remains score-active until a 168-hour clean window passes without recurrence.

sections.heading: Health score now reflects recent instability
sections.detail: Recent BSODs remain active during the clean-window period, and recent unexpected-shutdown/Kernel-Power history now also carries a health-score penalty. A maintenance run cannot restore 100/100 while recent crash evidence is still active.

sections.heading: WinGet source health check corrected
sections.detail: PulseGuard now runs `winget source list` without the unsupported `--accept-source-agreements` flag and treats help text, unrecognized-argument output, or malformed source-list output as unhealthy even if WinGet returns exit code 0.

sections.heading: Installed-app executable ownership hardened
sections.detail: A resolved executable is accepted as application-integrity evidence only when it is contained by the registered InstallLocation or, when outside it, has a valid Authenticode signature whose signer/company evidence matches the registered publisher. Unrelated executables such as cmd.exe or WindowsPackageManagerServer.exe can no longer make another application appear HEALTHY.

sections.heading: CPU accounting uses one sample
sections.detail: Total background CPU and required/optional/gaming/unknown/other components are now calculated from the same per-process sample, with the independent performance-counter average retained separately for context.

sections.heading: Startup optimization is safer
sections.detail: FIX + OPTIMIZE automatically changes only repair-like safe startup entries such as dead unowned targets. Ordinary user-installed app autostarts require an explicit Startup Manager action, and scheduled tasks tied to another Windows user SID are always protected.

sections.heading: Deep Clean no longer removes user recovery/cache data
sections.detail: Deep Clean no longer empties the Recycle Bin and no longer clears the DirectX shader cache. Recycle Bin size remains visible as preview-only information.

sections.heading: Game Ready reporting clarified
sections.detail: PARTIAL Game Ready decisions now explicitly separate which child processes were CLOSED and why from which were KEPT and why, removing contradictory-looking safety text.

sections.heading: Cleaner, consistent reports
sections.detail: Report serialization converts DateTime/DateTimeOffset values to ISO-8601 strings, omits the duplicated InstalledApps array when Rows already contains the same application inventory, and excludes bulky raw command-output fields from the consolidated JSON while retaining summarized evidence/log paths.

sections.heading: RAM slot labels and WinGet noise improved
sections.detail: RAM summary lines now include both bank and device-locator labels when available. WinGet packages previously proven NotApplicable for the exact same offered version are suppressed on later runs until the offered version changes.

sections.heading: Workflow wording corrected
sections.detail: The WinGet optimization step is now named for the verified application-upgrade workflow rather than implying that merely opening Command Prompt is the task.

sections.heading: Defender baseline visibility improved
sections.detail: Tamper Protection off and a never-recorded Defender full scan are now surfaced as separate informational findings. PulseGuard does not force-enable Tamper Protection or automatically launch a long full scan during routine optimization.
